chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Aban, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who divorces his wife with two divorces while in good health, then divorces the third time while he is ill. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She inherits him for as long as he remains in his illness, even if it lasts up to a year.'

key_terms.الثَّالِثَةَ: The third (divorce, which makes the divorce irrevocable)
key_terms.تَطْلِيقَتَيْنِ: Two divorces (referring to the first two revocable divorces)
key_terms.صِحَّةٍ: Health/Good health (state of being free from the specific illness)

ai.seo_question: Does a divorced wife inherit from her husband if he dies during his illness after the third divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the specific condition of 'deathbed divorce' (talaq al-marad) by establishing that the wife retains inheritance rights if the final divorce occurs while the husband is still in his terminal illness, regardless of whether he survives for a year or not. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of the marital bond during the illness period, distinguishing it from cases where divorce occurs after full recovery. This ruling ensures the wife's financial security is not compromised by a strategic delay in the finalization of the divorce.
